name: PlayerPrefsEditorWindow
src_typeComment: Toolkit/PlayerPrefs Editor: UnityEngine.PlayerPrefs has NO "list all keys" method, which makes a normal editor window impossible to build against it directly. On Windows, PlayerPrefs actually live in the registry under HKCU\Software\<Company>\<Product>, one value per key (named "<key>_h<hash>" — Unity appends a project-specific hash suffix to every key).  This tool reads THAT registry key purely to DISCOVER which keys exist (enumerate value names, strip the hash suffix) — it never parses Unity's undocumented on-disk VALUE format itself. Every actual read or write of a value goes through the real UnityEngine.PlayerPrefs API, which is guaranteed correct since it's Unity's own code doing the encoding/decoding, not a reverse-engineered guess at an undocumented binary layout — getting that wrong on a WRITE could silently corrupt real save data, which isn't a risk worth taking when the actual API is sitting right there to use instead.  Editor-only and WINDOWS-SPECIFIC by choice — macOS stores PlayerPrefs in a .plist and Linux in a config file, each needing its own discovery method this tool doesn't attempt.  The one place a real guess is unavoidable: distinguishing an Int/Float/String key from the registry alone, since PlayerPrefs.GetInt/GetFloat/GetString each need the CALLER to already know the type. CONFIRMED BY TESTING (not assumed): PlayerPrefs.SetInt AND PlayerPrefs.SetFloat both write a plain RegistryValueKind.DWord — Unity stores a float's raw 4 bytes reinterpreted as the DWord's bit pattern rather than tagging it Binary, so DWord alone CANNOT tell Int and Float apart; this is a routine ambiguity affecting every float key, not a rare edge case. Classified by value kind (DWord -> Int as a default guess, Binary -> String) with a manual "type" dropdown per row that is the ONLY reliable way to correctly view/edit a float key — flip it once and the row re-reads through PlayerPrefs.GetFloat instead, showing the real value.
